summary: Electric cars are set to pass 70% of China's car sales for the first time, a Dutch court blocks a BYD SUV in Europe over design copying, and Chinese tech stocks keep sliding.
body: China's car industry association expects 1.15 million electric and plug-in hybrid cars to be sold in November, 70.6% of all car sales and the eighth record month in a row.[^1] The share is rising mostly because petrol-car sales are collapsing, down an estimated 47% from a year ago; electric sales are also down about 13%.[^1] For families in China, this means most new cars bought now plug in.

On Nov 20 a court in The Hague ruled that BYD's Ti7 SUV copies the registered design of Jaguar Land Rover's Defender and issued a temporary ban on selling it in the EU or building it at BYD's new factory in Hungary.[^2][^3] BYD says it designed the car independently and will appeal. The ban does not cover the UK, and the ruling is provisional while the full case is heard.[^2][^3]

Chinese tech shares have lost about $1.7 trillion in value since the end of June, Bloomberg calculates, as investors worry about weak AI profits and a shortage of advanced chips after new US rules.[^4] Bloomberg notes that no Chinese model now ranks in the top 10 of one widely used AI benchmark.[^4] To support the market, China's three stock exchanges will lower the deposit needed to buy shares with borrowed money from 100% to 80% on Nov 30, reversing a January tightening.[^5]
differences: BYD and JLR disagree on whether the Ti7 copies the Defender; the court's ruling is temporary.[^2] On tech stocks, some fund managers think prices could fall much further, while Chinese firms say domestic chips are improving.[^4]

reads.title: China's $1.7 trillion AI rout turns once-hot tech trade into a losing bet
reads.summary: Why investors soured on China's AI companies this autumn, from chip shortages to slow profits, and how much of AI work runs on Nvidia versus Huawei chips.
